newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW-British interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-British interest rate rise.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to the decision of Britain's monetary policy committee to raise base rates by a quarter-point to 6.75 percent.

"The danger here is that the market will think it's not enough. The short sterling market is baying for blood. There will be some disappointment that they haven't gone for 50 (basis points). It opens the possiblity of more rises in the future."
"I think the Bank of England should have been rather more aggressive. The state of the economy calls for tougher action on interest rates. I think the market will probably react negatively."
"Pretty much as we expected. Because it was only 0.25 percent there might be some profit-taking. Wait for the next one."
"Some people (in the market) were expecting a half-point (rise). The market is out-performing at the short end."

"It's a missed opportunity. The Bank of England have been a little timid. As long as the forex market has something to look forward to, it's unlikey to offload its positions. By the year end we'll be looking at a rate of 7.25 percent.

"The danger is that they may be rebalancing the economy but at lower levels of growth and output. We may have to be dusting off the 'R' word, the recession word, as manufacturing slows down next year."
CHRIS GREENHALL, BRITISH CHAMBER OF COMMERCE:
"The manufacturing side is concerned. It will have a knock-on effect on jobs, profit and investment."

"Completely as expected. The Bank of England noted the well-above trend growth and sterling has sharpened the policy dilemma. Going on from here, there is more to come. It is difficult to know when the next one is going to come. They may hold on if they can and leave the next one until September."

"The 25-basis point hike by the Bank of England today was largely expected. But is unlikely to be deemed enough in the money markets to slow consumer spending to the pace needed to remove any inflation threat. To this end, many will look for another 25 basis points move at either the August and/or the September MPC meetings.
"We would certainly expect a 7 percent base rate by the end of this quarter."
